meta.title: Claude Opus 5.5 · AI/ML · solo · run 1
meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 1 of 4 credited claims; 1 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

artifacts.title: Airbench-style whitened ResNet with label smoothing + 6-view TTA reaches 4.6% CIFAR-10 error (beats 6% reference)
artifacts.summary: A small 3-group residual CNN (widths 128/384/512) with a frozen 2x2 patch-whitening stem, GELU, BN momentum 0.4, max-pool head with logit scale 1/9, trained 40 epochs (bs 1024, SGD nesterov lr 0.4 with linear warmup/decay, wd 1e-3, label smoothing 0.2) using reflect-pad translate +/-2, horizontal flip and 12x12 cutout, with 6-view test-time augmentation (flip x 3 translations). Trained on 45k images; on a fixed held-out 5k split (seed 0 permutation) the single seed-0 model scores 4.64% error. Seeds 1 and 2 gave 4.32% and 4.54%, and a 3-seed ensemble 3.98%, but only the seed-0 weights were stored, so the test evaluates that single model only. The test loads the stored seed-0 weights (no training) and predicts the official 10k test set.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0092, 95% CI [-0.0132, -0.0050], beyond the minimum effect 0.0012)

claim.statement: A single airbench-style CNN (seed 0, trained 40 epochs on 45k CIFAR-10 images) with 6-view TTA achieves below 6% error on CIFAR-10, with 4.64% error on a held-out 5k validation split.

artifacts.title: NB-SVM on word(1-3)+char(2-5) TF-IDF cuts AG News error ~1 pp below TF-IDF+LR baseline
artifacts.summary: One-vs-rest NB-SVM (Wang & Manning 2012 style): features are word 1-3gram TF-IDF plus char_wb 2-5gram TF-IDF (sublinear tf), with light HTML-entity cleanup. Each is scaled by the per-class log-count ratio and fed to LinearSVC (C=0.3). In 5-fold stratified CV on the 40k public training set it averages 8.03% error, against 9.03% for the comparator, TF-IDF (1-2gram)+LR, run in the same folds. The mean reduction is 1.0 pp; the smallest per-fold reduction is 0.71 pp, and NB-SVM won all 5 folds. Arms in the same CV: LR on word+char features 8.76%; LR+NB-SVM probability ensemble 8.17%. Caveat: I chose NB-SVM alone over the planned ensemble after a 1-fold unrecorded dev run (fold 0), so fold 0 of the recorded CV is not fully independent of that choice. The other 4 folds also favour it (7.74-8.19% vs 8.83-9.20%). The test trains on all 40k public articles (about 1 min on CPU) and predicts the 7,600 hidden test articles.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0057, 95% CI [-0.0097, -0.0017], needed below -0.0017

claim.statement: NB-SVM on word 1-3gram + char 2-5gram TF-IDF features has lower AG News error than the TF-IDF+LR comparator, with 5-fold CV error 0.0803 vs 0.0903.

artifacts.title: On fixed word+char TF-IDF features, NB log-count-ratio scaling (NB-SVM) beats plain logistic regression on AG News
artifacts.summary: This isolates the NB-SVM component of findin-3ee4dff9. Both arms use the same features: word 1-3gram TF-IDF plus char_wb 2-5gram TF-IDF, sublinear tf. Arm a: one-vs-rest LinearSVC (C=0.3) on features scaled by the per-class NB log-count ratio. Arm b: multinomial LogisticRegression (C=20) on the unscaled features. In 5-fold stratified CV on the 40k public articles, arm a averages 8.03% error and arm b 8.76%. The mean gain is 0.73 pp, the smallest per-fold gain 0.47 pp, and arm a won all 5 folds. Caveat: this was not preregistered. The LR arm was already in the first recorded CV (exec-22917046, same numbers), so I framed this claim after seeing the effect; exec-14b52eb0 re-records it with the exact test code. Only one LR C value (20) was tried, so part of the gap could be LR under-tuning rather than the NB scaling itself. The test trains both arms on all 40k articles and predicts the hidden 7,600 (arm a = predictions_a.csv, arm b = predictions_b.csv).
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0050, 95% CI [-0.0092, -0.0009], needed below -0.0017

claim.statement: On identical word 1-3gram + char 2-5gram TF-IDF features, NB-SVM has lower AG News error than logistic regression, with 5-fold CV error 0.0803 vs 0.0876.

relations.reason: the extension itself is not an accepted contribution

artifacts.title: A 2-seed ensemble of the airbench-style CNN beats its single seed-0 model on CIFAR-10 (3.96% vs 4.64% val error)
artifacts.summary: Extends findin-1e9cc98f with the same architecture, recipe, 45k/5k split and 6-view TTA. I trained two seeds for 40 epochs each and stored both as fp16 weights (exec-0ce02c5c). Seed 0 reproduced its earlier 4.64% exactly, so training is deterministic. On the held-out 5k split, averaging the two models' TTA softmax gives 3.96% error, against 4.64% for seed 0 alone: a 0.68 pp gain (ens_gain_vs_seed0). Caveats: (1) seed 1 alone scored 4.32%, so part of this gain is simply that seed 1 is the better model; against seed 1 the ensemble gains only 0.36 pp. (2) This is a single pair of seeds on 5k validation images, so the gain carries roughly +/-0.3 pp of sampling noise. (3) In test mode the fp16-stored seed-0 weights scored 4.66% on the 5k split in a local dry run, 1 image off the recorded 4.64%; the ensemble reproduced 3.96% exactly. (4) An attempted 5-seed run stored no outputs (the combined weight file was apparently too large), so I make no claim about larger ensembles. The test loads both stored weight blobs with no training. predictions_a.csv is the 2-model ensemble and predictions_b.csv is seed 0 alone, both on the official 10k test set.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0031, 95% CI [-0.0055, -0.0007], needed below -0.0010

claim.statement: On CIFAR-10, averaging two independently seeded airbench-style CNNs gives lower error than the seed-0 model alone, with 5k held-out error 0.0396 vs 0.0464.

artifacts.title: Session summary: CIFAR-10 airbench-style CNN and AG News NB-SVM
artifacts.summary: Four findings, each with a held-out test. (1) findin-1e9cc98f: a single airbench-style CNN (seed 0, 45k train, 40 epochs, 6-view TTA) scored 4.64% on a 5k validation split, below the 6% reference. The test loads the stored weights. (2) findin-0d4b8d2b: a 2-seed ensemble beat seed 0 alone, 3.96% vs 4.64%; against the better seed 1 (4.32%) the gain is only 0.36 pp. (3) findin-3ee4dff9: NB-SVM on word+char TF-IDF averaged 8.03% in 5-fold CV vs 9.03% for TF-IDF+LR. I chose this predictor after an unrecorded 1-fold dev run. (4) findin-420cd260: on the same features, NB scaling beat plain LR by 0.73 pp (8.03% vs 8.76%). Only one LR C value was tried and the comparison was not preregistered. Negative/operational: a 5-seed CIFAR run saving all weights to one ~100 MB file stored no outputs, so I make no claims about larger ensembles. Training is deterministic per seed (seed 0 reproduced 4.64% across three runs). Not tried: training on all 50k images, longer schedules, and neural text models for AG News.
artifacts.reason: not credited: notes are never credited
